The test image shows a severely wilted, brown/tan, dried-out mango leaf that has curled and shriveled along its length. The entire leaf is affected — uniformly brown, desiccated, with no green remaining. This suggests dieback or severe blight affecting the whole leaf.

Now let me view one reference from each class.
Strong match — Die_Back reference shows the same uniformly brown, shriveled, curled mango leaf on a white background. Very similar appearance.
Anthracnose reference shows a partially affected leaf — still has some yellow-green areas with brown lesions, not fully shriveled. Less similar to the test image.
Powdery Mildew shows white powdery patches on a green leaf — clearly different from the test image.

Sooty Mould shows black sooty deposits on a green leaf — clearly different.

Now let me get more Die_Back references to confirm the match.
Another strong Die_Back match — same uniformly brown, desiccated, curled/shriveled leaf form.

Die_Back_383 is another perfect match — same compact, fully brown, shriveled leaf on white background, identical to the test image. Anthracnose_383 shows discrete dark lesions on a green leaf — completely different.

All 8 views used. The evidence is conclusive.

**Summary:**
- Die_Back references (all 3): uniformly brown, desiccated, shriveled/curled leaves — identical to test image
- Anthracnose: partial brown lesions/spots on green/yellow leaves — different
- Powdery_Mildew: white powder on green leaves — different
- Sooty_Mould: black deposits on green leaves — different
